title: Analysis
blurb: Accuracy counting, paired tests and metrics.

blocks.name: slmjury.analysis.accuracy
blocks.lead: Accuracy counts for judgement files, computed the way JudgeEvaluator and the summaries compute them.

about.html: Per file, Undefined verdicts stay in the denominator; across files, counts are summed before dividing. Importing this module changes no global state. Analyses turn on strict MATH labels themselves.

blocks.name: Counts
blocks.summary: Raw counts for one judgement file, the unit of micro-averaging.

blocks.name: file_counts
blocks.summary: Counts for one judgement file, computed by `JudgeEvaluator`.

body.html: Returns None when the file is absent, empty or unreadable, so callers can tell "not run" from "run and scored 0".

blocks.name: micro
blocks.summary: Micro-average a collection of `Counts`; None entries are skipped.

blocks.name: verdict_pairs
blocks.summary: (judge verdict, expected verdict) for every record, both lower-cased.

body.html: Both values come from the same record, so the pairs stay aligned even when files differ in length.

blocks.name: expected_verdict
blocks.summary: Expected verdict ("correct"/"incorrect") and student answer for one record.

body.html: Same logic as `JudgeEvaluator._get_expected_verdict`, for analyses that need a label per item rather than an aggregate.

blocks.name: slmjury.analysis.stats
blocks.lead: Significance tests and intervals for comparing judges: McNemar, cluster bootstrap, TOST, BH, Wilson.

about.html: Needs only the standard library; numpy, when present, speeds up the bootstrap. Self-test (also checks against scipy when it is installed): python -m slmjury.analysis.stats

blocks.name: McNemarResult
blocks.sig: (b: 'int', c: 'int', n_discordant: 'int', n_pairs: 'int', p_exact: 'float', p_midp: 'float', p_chi2_cc: 'float', odds_ratio: 'float') -> None
blocks.summary: McNemarResult(b: 'int', c: 'int', n_discordant: 'int', n_pairs: 'int', p_exact: 'float', p_midp: 'float', p_chi2_cc: 'float', odds_ratio: 'float')

blocks.name: BootstrapResult
blocks.sig: (point: 'float', lo: 'float', hi: 'float', se: 'float', alpha: 'float', n_boot: 'int', n_items: 'int', n_clusters: 'int', clusters: 'list' = <factory>) -> None
blocks.summary: BootstrapResult(point: 'float', lo: 'float', hi: 'float', se: 'float', alpha: 'float', n_boot: 'int', n_items: 'int', n_clusters: 'int', clusters: 'list' = <factory>)

blocks.name: mcnemar
blocks.summary: Exact two-sided McNemar test on two paired per-item correctness vectors.

body.html: Under the null, the discordant pairs are Binomial(b + c, 1/2). Concordant pairs say nothing about which judge is better and drop out.

blocks.name: discordant_counts
blocks.summary: (b, c, n): b = a right and b wrong, c = a wrong and b right, n = items.

body.html: Both arguments are per-item 0/1 sequences over the same items in the same order; aligning them is the caller's job.

blocks.name: cluster_bootstrap_diff
blocks.summary: Percentile CI on (accuracy_a - accuracy_b), in accuracy points.

body.html: Items are resampled with replacement within each cluster (normally the dataset), and cluster sizes stay fixed: items within a dataset are exchangeable, while the dataset sizes are set by the study design.

blocks.name: tost_equivalence
blocks.sig: (a_correct, b_correct, clusters, margin_points: 'float' = 0.5, alpha: 'float' = 0.05, n_boot: 'int' = 10000, seed: 'int' = 20260916) -> 'dict'
blocks.summary: Two one-sided tests: is |accuracy_a - accuracy_b| smaller than `margin_points`?

body.html: Same as the (1 - 2*alpha) bootstrap CI lying inside +-margin (the 90% CI at alpha = 0.05). The margin and the differences are in accuracy points, as are the `_pp` keys of the result.

blocks.name: bootstrap_ci
blocks.summary: Percentile CI for any statistic of a list of items, resampled i.i.d.

blocks.name: spearman_bootstrap_ci
blocks.summary: CI on Spearman rho, with (x, y) pairs resampled together.

body.html: rho comes from slmjury.core.scoring_evaluator, as in the scoring pipeline, so the interval is around the reported value. The import is lazy, to keep this module free of package imports at load time.

blocks.name: benjamini_hochberg
blocks.summary: Benjamini-Hochberg step-up procedure. Returns q-values and which tests survive.

blocks.name: macro_micro
blocks.summary: Micro and macro averages from (correct, total) pairs, one pair per group.

body.html: Micro weights every item equally, so large datasets dominate it; macro weights every group (dataset) equally.

blocks.name: wilson_interval
blocks.summary: Wilson score interval for one proportion, in percentage points.

body.html: Meant for a single judge's accuracy. A difference between two judges on the same items is paired and needs the bootstrap above.

blocks.name: slmjury.analysis.metrics
blocks.lead: Correlation, agreement and ranking metrics used by the analyses.

about.html: pearson, spearman, cohens_kappa, the evaluate_* functions and save_evaluation are re-exported from slmjury.core.scoring_evaluator. Self-test: python -m slmjury.analysis.metrics

blocks.name: kendall_tau
blocks.summary: Kendall tau (tau-a) between two rankings of the same items.

blocks.name: rank_stability
blocks.summary: Pairwise Kendall tau between the judge rankings of each prompt variant.

body.html: `accuracy_by_variant` maps each variant to per-judge accuracies, all in the same judge order. Returns {"mean_tau", "min_tau", "pairwise": {(v1, v2): tau}}.

blocks.name: false_accept_rate
blocks.summary: Share of truly incorrect items the judge labelled correct (lower-cased labels).

blocks.name: false_reject_rate
blocks.summary: Share of truly correct items the judge did not label correct.

blocks.name: far_frr_matrix
blocks.summary: FAR, FRR and accuracy for every judge and student, over items with a Correct/Incorrect verdict.

body.html: Takes {judge: {student: [judgement dicts]}} and the expected verdicts {student: ["correct" | "incorrect"]}; returns {judge: {student: {"far", "frr", "accuracy"}}}.

blocks.name: position_bias_flip_rate
blocks.summary: Share of items where the judge's preference changes when A and B are swapped.

body.html: A consistent judge answers "A" in one run and "B" in the other. Only items with an A/B answer in both runs count; 0 is fully consistent, 0.5 is what random answers give.

blocks.name: pareto_front
blocks.summary: Pareto-optimal subset of (cost, quality, label) points, sorted by cost.

blocks.name: slmjury.analysis.scoring
blocks.lead: Open-ended metrics (SummEval, MT-Bench) without intermediate rounding.

about.html: The scoring evaluator rounds each metric, and so the SummEval `overall` means, to four decimals. These helpers run its own functions on the raw records with rounding turned off, so each value is rounded once, when printed.

blocks.name: summeval
blocks.summary: `evaluate_summeval` on raw SummEval records, without rounding.

blocks.name: mtbench
blocks.summary: `evaluate_mtbench` on raw MT-Bench records, without rounding.

blocks.name: slmjury.analysis.pairwise
blocks.lead: Read the letter ("A" or "B") a pairwise judge committed to.

about.html: Reasoning judges explain first, some decline to choose, and the article "a" is not a vote, so `read_choice` accepts only a committed choice. Anything else is "Undefined" and is left out of the flip rate.

blocks.name: read_choice
blocks.summary: The letter ("A" or "B") a pairwise judge committed to, or "Undefined".

blocks.name: slmjury.analysis.paths
blocks.lead: Where analysis scripts find their inputs and write their outputs.

about.html: Everything lives under one results folder, `$SLMJURY_RESULTS if set, else ./results. core and experiment raise MissingResults` with the expected path, so a missing input fails at once.

blocks.name: MissingResults
blocks.summary: An expected results file or folder does not exist.

blocks.name: results_dir
blocks.summary: The results root: `$SLMJURY_RESULTS if set, else ./results`.

blocks.name: default_dir
blocks.summary: A folder under the results root, as a string for a runner's CLI default.

blocks.name: core
blocks.summary: `results/core/<name> for one of the folders in CORE_NAMES`.

blocks.name: experiment
blocks.summary: `results/<name>`, the raw runs of one experiment.

blocks.name: analysis_dir
blocks.summary: `results/analysis/<name>`, created if it does not exist.

blocks.name: analysis_figures_dir
blocks.summary: `results/figures/analysis/<name>`, created if it does not exist.

blocks.name: cache_dir
blocks.summary: `results/cache/<name>`, created if it does not exist.

blocks.name: require
blocks.summary: Return `path if it exists, else raise MissingResults`.
